question: Can a Zustand persist hydration that began before clearStorage() still apply the cleared stored snapshot to live state?

sources.name: Pinned Zustand persist source
sources.claim: Hydration generations invalidate older rehydrate work, while clearStorage did not advance the generation.

sources.name: Accepted clear-storage candidate
sources.claim: The candidate advances the existing hydration generation before storage removal and covers stale state, observer, later-hydration, and synchronous-removal-failure behavior.

sources.name: Exact candidate execution carrier
sources.claim: Exact source identity, two-file fence, repository formatting, types, lint, specs, diff hygiene, and clean tree passed.

command: pnpm run test:format && pnpm run test:types && pnpm run test:lint && pnpm run test:spec

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: A delayed read or migration from a pre-clear hydration can publish under the pinned source.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: clearStorage did not previously revoke the active hydration generation.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: The candidate suppresses delayed state and lifecycle publication after clear.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Advancing the existing generation transfers publication authority to the clear intent.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: A synchronous removeItem failure still leaves the old hydration revoked.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Logical clear authority is independent from physical removal success.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: A later hydration succeeds and publishes state and completion signals exactly once.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The repair revokes only older work and preserves future hydration.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: Complete repository format, type, lint, and spec gates pass at the exact candidate head.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The selected two-file source is technically ready within the tested repository boundary.

stop_condition: Stop after exact-head target execution, lifecycle and removal-failure policy controls, complete two-file review, and carrier retirement.
